subject: Implement composition resolution in core: revision vector, exact-pin closure, read-only imports, agreement checks, cycles, composed readiness and impact; move bundle publishing into core
description:
WHY: the spec's sections on agreements, exports and references; contract and release binding; and changes across repositories (impact). Acceptance scenarios: parent with nested components, missing child or wrong digest, child contract change, runtime interaction cycle.

GROUNDING:
- bundleFor falls back to a match without a version (rules/versions.ts:65); pinnedBundle is exact (:68-72); publishedRules :75-108.
- References `<pinId>:<recordId>` (refs.ts:36-41) resolve as external (:65-70).
- Readiness for pins: readiness.ts:278-296, task classes :317. Scope through consumers: scope.ts:45-46, :138.
- Only OpenAPI reports import coverage (projections/openapi.ts:82-113).
- Frozen components exist: the baseline's `frozen` flag or policy `freeze.onAcceptance` (baseline.ts:96), with FROZEN_COMPONENT_CHANGED raised at baseline.ts:123 (rule at codes.ts:136).
- The designer builds bundles itself (apps/designer/src/app/loom-store.ts:446-471).
- Task 5 contracts: RecordAddress {modelId, kind, id}, ResolvedReference, ContractPin, Agreement (providers[] and consumers[] as RecordAddress), ExportBundle (allOf PublishedContract plus modelId, sourceCommit, agreementBundle and the closure members), AgreementBundle, AgreementBinding, RevisionVector, ChangeProposal, CompositionRelease. Model carries no modelId of its own; the identity comes from LoomConfig.modelId (optional until task 14).

CHANGE (new core module composition.ts):
- Resolution: a deterministic revision vector; closure resolution through exact pins only; records addressed as {modelId, kind, id} plus the bundle digest. The model's own id is a resolution input (from the workspace's LoomConfig), since Model has none.
- Read-only imports: mutate refuses a patch to an imported record and returns the owner and the next action.
- Agreements: the parent's Agreement records versus the provider export, and consumer binding to the exact export plus its mapping records. An export missing part of its required closure cannot qualify its consumer.
- With the model's own id available, each component's ICD lists the agreements its records provide or consume (found in task 5: the ICD view cannot tell local addresses from foreign ones without it).
- Parent checks: agreement satisfaction, consumer closure, deployment fit (export hosting requirements against the parent's deployment units), authorization crossings, workflows and integration evidence.
- Composed rules in both directions: a passing parent never replaces a failing child, and a passing child never proves end-to-end behaviour.
- Cycles: ownership and artifact-reference cycles fail with the cycle path; runtime call cycles are allowed; explicit depth and size limits.
- Composed readiness:
  - Empty export pins block dependent implementation and release, not unrelated work.
  - The incomplete-journal block is a pure rule over the journal state passed in as input. Task 15 integrates it with real journals and re-verifies it.
- Traversal: context and impact cross members and keep the source owner. Impact names affected owners, consumers, frozen components, generated artifacts and invalidated evidence.
- Frozen scope: extend the FROZEN_COMPONENT_CHANGED evaluation to cross-model plans, so requiredAcceptance shows the affected frozen scope and the exact policy obligation.
- Import coverage: imported records are reported by every projection that renders them.
- A core function builds agreement and export bundles. The designer publish (and views.spec) switches to it; CLI and federation reuse it.
- Tests include a parent workflow resolving through an exact child export.
- New codes: FindingCode, FINDING_RULES, CONTRADICTIONS. Comparison rules: DIFF_RULES, FIELD_POLICY, a diffs.ts case.

AREA TESTS: npm run build; core battery. From apps/designer: npm run build; npx ng test --watch=false --include src/app/views.spec.ts; npx ng test --watch=false --include src/app/states.spec.ts.
WORKER: loom-worker (Sonnet 5, effort high, as its definition sets), resumed across its milestone while its context allows (task 1, warm reuse); Opus at xhigh only through `ledger escalate <task>` when the task proves complex, meaning an unresolved design question or a defect the worker cannot land (owner rule: prefer Sonnet; Opus xhigh only for complex work).
